bluf: Amplify, the Copenhagen agency that webamp.dk now resolves to, is a founder led full service shop run by Nicolai Vittrup, founder and CEO, selling small businesses an external marketing department across SEO, Google Ads, social and web design. The record shows an undated rename and a case library dated 2022-05-16 to 2024-08-01, with nothing in the sitemap updated in 90 days, so where it is going is not on file. Its book holds 9 clients, 6 observed and 3 names only. A rival should know the Horus read puts it in the Exposed band and its own house practises 1 of the 3 lines tested.
doing:
Amplify sells an outsourced marketing department to small businesses. Its positioning line, a Copenhagen full service digital marketing agency working as clients' external marketing department, pairing strategy and branding with performance execution, means: it plans the brand, then runs the ads, the search work and the site for firms without their own team. The headline claim is one featured case: it says it lifted both brand and bottom line for the Zealand removals firm Mesterflyt, with no figure given. The founder and CEO is Nicolai Vittrup; the record lists no founding year or headcount and one office, Copenhagen.

The sold mix has no lead line; SEO, Paid Search, Paid Social and Web & Product score 2 and form the core. The evidence is the case tags: all seven tagged cases include SEO, six of seven are tagged Web, including Acture and A2Vent, five of seven carry Social Ads, and the Nordic Tea case pairs SEO with Google Ads, a service spanning Search, Shopping and Display. The service list adds strategy, branding, 360° marketing and video and visual content. AI Search / GEO, Content & Digital PR, Creator & Influencer and Programmatic & CTV score 1 without notes; Data & Measurement, CRO, Email & CRM and AI Automation score 0. The record lists no proprietary product and no partner.

Its AI posture is content, not product: it frames SEO as visibility in search engines and LLMs and publishes AEO and ChatGPT guides, with no AI service line. The one move on record is the rename from webamp.dk to amplify.dk, undated. The case library runs from Nordic Tea (2022-05-16) and A2Vent (2022-06-17) through Bernstorff Slot (2023-03-16), Collectia (2023-05-13) and OLIOLI (2023-06-20) to Acture (2024-04-26) and Nellemann Leasing (2024-08-01). The record lists no pricing signal, news or open roles, though a careers page exists. Conspicuously absent for an agency sold as the client's whole marketing department: any data, measurement, CRM or email line.
clients:
The client type is SMB, across automotive leasing, healthcare, hospitality and conference venues, industrial B2B (ventilation), ecommerce and removals, sold from Copenhagen. The needs read holds 9 clients, 6 observed and 3 names only, all from client testimonial cases; brand and creative and local and lead generation lead the mix (2 clients each).

Acture, formerly Health Group, came for leads: the case claims it created leads and higher revenue (2024-04-26). Nellemann Leasing came for brand and creative, branding and marketing strategy with a focus on execution, its title promising premium across channels (2024-08-01). Collectia came for brand: a new visual identity and websites for a stronger brand and usability (2023-05-13). Nordic Tea came for paid performance and organic demand: SEO and Google Ads together lifting visibility on Google and webshop revenue (2022-05-16). OLIOLI took a 360 degree channel mix for a clear digital strategy (2023-06-20).

Three readings are judgment calls. Acture is counted twice, once as Acture (formerly Health Group), on the same case URL. The AI and automation code on OLIOLI has no visible basis in its excerpt. And the 3 names only all carry described work: the headline credits Mesterflyt with a lifted brand and bottom line, the Bernstorff Slot case describes a 360 degree channel mix for a conference venue (2023-03-16), and the A2Vent case says online results carried into revenue (2022-06-17). No client is shared with another tracked agency.

Under KJ4 (the platforms absorbing the execution layer) it is likely, moderate confidence, that clients buying Google Ads and social ads from it, Nordic Tea among them, will see platform automation take over that work; under KJ1 its SEO clients likely need visibility in LLM answers, which it writes about but does not sell as a line (low confidence).
house: Say and do: three lines tested, one practised. Paid social is contradicted: it sells paid and organic social and runs no social ad pixel on its own site. LinkedIn advertising is contradicted: the LinkedIn check finds 0 ads ("0 ads match the name query"). Paid search is unknown: the Transparency Center lookup was blocked, so no Google count or sample line exists. Publishing cadence is marked corroborated on 10 sitemap URLs updated in 365 days, but 0 of its 336 URLs were updated in 90 days and the record lists no recent blog dates: the machine has been quiet for a quarter. The tag stack is GTM and HubSpot on WordPress and Elementor, with no test tools and no ABM stack. It publishes no llms.txt, blocks no AI crawlers and has 3 AI topic URLs. Its social profiles run on LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook.
market:
The Horus read puts Amplify at a tailwind index of -11.6, band Exposed, percentile 7. It is best placed for KJ1 (the click replaced by the citation) and KJ2 (ads inside AI answers), both driven by AI Search / GEO and Paid Search. It is most exposed to KJ4 (the platforms absorbing the execution layer), driven by Paid Search and Paid Social, and KJ6 (the agency middle hollowed out), driven by Paid Search, Paid Social and SEO. Best scenario fit: The Toll Road at 42/100. It is partial on P1 and P4, absent on P2, P6, P7 and P8, unknown on P5; P3 does not apply.

The Monsoon read is 63.4, band Onshore wind, percentile 81: migration 57.4 against displacement 69.4. The sold mix supplies 57 of the index, SEO (15) and Web & Product (15) carrying the most movable hours, and automation overlaps 28% of them; the work would go 50% to South and Southeast Asia and 40% to Eastern Europe. The footprint is inferred, with no hub office and no onshore claim.
openings:
The strongest opening is price and freshness together. Displacement at 69.4 says the book buys on price, the SMB client type adds 12 points to that read, and no case is dated after 2024-08-01 while the sitemap shows 0 updates in 90 days. It is likely, moderate confidence, that its SMB accounts, the 2022 clients A2Vent and Nordic Tea first, are contestable by a rival offering SEO, Google Ads and site builds at a lower rate with current, figured proof. Falsifier: new dated 2026 cases with figures in the next compile.

Its own house undercuts its social pitch: it sells paid social and LinkedIn with no social ad pixel and 0 LinkedIn ads of its own, so a rival showing live social programmes very likely wins that comparison. The record shows no feed, schema or entity work (P2 absent), no test of ads inside assistants (P8 absent) and no public pricing (P5 unknown): a rival selling AI answer visibility as a measured product meets an agency that only publishes guides about it.
watch: I7, holiday 2026 agentic checkout volume and merchant opt out rates, December 2026 to January 2027: high opt out rates would slow KJ4, the judgment its paid search and paid social lines are most exposed to.
I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures, October 2026: outcome pricing at a top five holdco would sharpen KJ6 against an agency with no public pricing.
I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, late October 2026: growth above 15% with AI Mode ads live would confirm S1 and the KJ1 tailwind, its best placed judgment.
I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility, late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth would confirm the UGC starvation risk under KJ1.
The undated rename from webamp.dk to amplify.dk and the sitemap at 0 updates in 90 days: new dated cases or posts under the Amplify name would show whether the rebrand is a relaunch or a pause.
The next Radar compile: this dossier is only as fresh as the 2026-09-28 compile, and the blocked Transparency Center lookup leaves its Google ads unknown.
